```{julia}

using Pkg
Pkg.activate(joinpath(@__DIR__, "../../../AmberMakie/docs"))
using Amber, AmberMakie, CairoMakie
CairoMakie.activate!()
```

Amber's equation-oriented core is not limited to electronics. Any system that
can be expressed as conservation laws plus constitutive relations can use the
same nonlinear compiler and transient solver. Here, capacitor voltages encode
the four states of the classic space-clamped Hodgkin--Huxley membrane.

## Map differential equations onto a circuit

One-farad capacitors make KCL read directly as $dx/dt=f(x)$. Membrane voltage
is stored in volts and the dimensionless gate fractions are represented as
voltages with the convention 1 V = 1 V/V.

```{julia}
@circuit ProjectHodgkinHuxley(; stimulus=10.0) begin
    gnd = ground()
    membrane = node(); m_gate = node(); h_gate = node(); n_gate = node()

    Cm = capacitor(membrane, gnd; value=1.0)
    Cmg = capacitor(m_gate, gnd; value=1.0)
    Chg = capacitor(h_gate, gnd; value=1.0)
    Cng = capacitor(n_gate, gnd; value=1.0)
    for state in (membrane, m_gate, h_gate, n_gate)
        resistor(state, gnd; value=1e15)
    end

    vtrap(x, y) = abs(x/y) < 1e-6 ? y*(1 - x/(2y)) : x/expm1(x/y)
    rates(v) = begin
        vm = 1e3v
        (0.1vtrap(25-vm, 10), 4exp(-vm/18),
         0.07exp(-vm/20), inv(exp((30-vm)/10)+1),
         0.01vtrap(10-vm, 10), 0.125exp(-vm/80))
    end
    dynamics(x, _) = begin
        v, m, h, n = x
        am, bm, ah, bh, an, bn = rates(v)
        ina = 120m^3*h*(1e3v-115)
        ik = 36n^4*(1e3v+12)
        il = 0.3*(1e3v-10.613)
        (stimulus-ina-ik-il,
         1e3*(am*(1-m)-bm*m),
         1e3*(ah*(1-h)-bh*h),
         1e3*(an*(1-n)-bn*n))
    end
    function jacobian_row(row, x, t)
        epsilon = 1e-6
        base = dynamics(x, t)[row]
        ntuple(j -> begin
            shifted = Base.setindex(x, x[j] + epsilon, j)
            (dynamics(shifted, t)[row] - base)/epsilon
        end, 4)
    end

    controls = ((membrane,gnd), (m_gate,gnd), (h_gate,gnd), (n_gate,gnd))
    for (row, output) in enumerate((membrane, m_gate, h_gate, n_gate))
        behavioral_current_source(controls, output, gnd;
            current=(x,t)->-dynamics(x,t)[row],
            gradient=(x,t)->.-jacobian_row(row,x,t))
    end

    initial_voltage(Cm, -65mV)
    initial_voltage(Cmg, 0.053)
    initial_voltage(Chg, 0.596)
    initial_voltage(Cng, 0.318)
    observe(membrane); observe(m_gate); observe(h_gate); observe(n_gate)
end
```

The behavioral sources receive all four state values. Supplying their Jacobian
rows lets Amber's Newton solver use the coupling explicitly instead of relying
on opaque black-box integration.

```{julia}
response = transient(ProjectHodgkinHuxley(), 0s => 20ms; max_step=20μs)
membrane_voltage = voltage(response, :membrane)
peak_index = argmax(membrane_voltage)

(
    resting_voltage=first(membrane_voltage),
    peak_voltage=membrane_voltage[peak_index],
    peak_time=response.axis[peak_index],
    converged=response.stats[:converged],
)
```

## Watch the action potential and its gating variables

```{julia}
figure = Figure(size=(1050, 780))
traceplot(figure[1, 1], response; signals=:membrane, color="#D55E00")
traceplot(figure[2, 1], response;
    signals=[:m_gate, :h_gate, :n_gate])
Label(figure[0, 1], "Hodgkin–Huxley action potential and ion-channel gates";
    fontsize=21)
figure
```

The fast sodium activation gate `m` opens first, producing the rising edge.
Sodium inactivation `h` falls while potassium activation `n` rises, returning
the membrane toward rest. Amber is solving this with the same compilation,
sparse nonlinear machinery, result accessors, and plotting adapters used by
the converter and oscillator projects.

::: {.callout-note}
This formulation demonstrates a general modeling technique, not a claim that
gate fractions are electrical voltages. The circuit variables are a convenient
coordinate system for a coupled differential-algebraic solver.
:::
